propositions.text: The Principal Applicant and his minor children seek judicial review of an officer's refusal of an open work permit application.
propositions.quote: Mr. Paul Uchemadu Adiele (the “Principal Applicant”) and his minor children Wisdom Ugonna Adiele-Paul, Miracle Nneoma Adiele-Paul, and Praise Chidera Adiele-Paul (collectively “the Applicants”) seek judicial review of the decision of an officer (the “Officer”) refusing his application for an open work permit

propositions.text: The open work permit was to accompany his wife, a student at the University of Saskatchewan.
propositions.quote: in order to accompany his wife, a student at the University of Saskatchewan.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicants seek judicial review of an officer's refusal of an open work permit to accompany the wife studying at University of Saskatchewan.

propositions.text: The Principal Applicant's application was refused on February 2, 2024 for insufficient evidence that his wife was a full-time student at a DLI.
propositions.quote: The Principal Applicant’s application was refused on February 2, 2024, on the grounds that there was insufficient evidence submitted to show that his wife was a full-time student at a Designated Learning Institution (“DLI”)

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker refused the application on February 2, 2024 due to insufficient evidence of wife's full-time student status at a DLI.

propositions.text: On February 5, 2024, the Principal Applicant requested reconsideration of the refusal decision.
propositions.quote: On February 5, 2024, the Principal Applicant requested reconsideration of the decision.

propositions.text: On February 7, 2024, IRCC acknowledged receipt of reconsideration request and stated no response within 10 working days means refusal of reconsideration.
propositions.quote: Thank you for your correspondence. We acknowledge receipt of your reconsideration request. We will contact you if there is a change in the status of your application. If you do not hear from us in 10 working days, then you should consider your request to have your application reconsidered on the grounds you presented in your request to have been refused.

propositions.text: IRCC advised reapplication is possible and new applications are decided on their own merits.
propositions.quote: You may re-apply if you wish, according to the regulations, fees, and forms requirements in effect at the time you reapply. Any new application will be decided on its own merits based on the supporting evidence submitted with that application and the regulations in force at the time.

propositions.text: IRCC stated this information suffices in response to the enquiry.
propositions.quote: We trust that this information suffices in responding to your enquiry.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the Principal Applicant requested reconsideration and IRCC acknowledged it, stating no response in 10 days means refusal and reapplication is possible.

propositions.text: The Principal Applicant deposed he did not hear further from IRCC within 10 days about reconsideration.
propositions.quote: the Principal Applicant deposed that he did not hear further from IRCC within 10 days about the reconsideration request.

propositions.text: He filed his application for leave and judicial review about the February 2, 2024 decision on February 29, 2024.
propositions.quote: He filed his application for leave and judicial review about the February 2, 2024 decision on February 29, 2024.

paragraphs.summary: The Principal Applicant deposed he received no further response within 10 days and filed for judicial review on February 29, 2024.

propositions.text: On October 21, 2024, IRCC determined sufficient evidence showed spouse was full-time student at a DLI.
propositions.quote: On October 21, 2024, IRCC sent the Principal Applicant an email advising that it had been determined that there was sufficient evidence to show that his spouse was a full-time student at a DLI in Canada.

propositions.text: However, the open work permit application remained refused based on funds.
propositions.quote: However, the Principal Applicant’s application for an open work permit “remains refused based on funds”.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker later found sufficient evidence of spouse's full-time student status but refused the permit based on funds.

propositions.text: Following a Production Order, IRCC filed the Certified Tribunal Record (CTR).
propositions.quote: Following the issuance of a Production Order on June 26, 2024, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (“IRCC”) filed the Certified Tribunal Record (the “CTR”).

propositions.text: The Respondent objected to inclusion in the CTR of materials relating to the reconsideration request.
propositions.quote: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (the “Respondent”) objected to the inclusion in that CTR of materials relating to the Principal Applicant’s request for reconsideration of the February 2, 2024 decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes IRCC filed the CTR after a Production Order and the Respondent objected to including reconsideration materials.

propositions.text: An amended CTR was filed excluding materials about the reconsideration request.
propositions.quote: An amended CTR was filed on November 7, 2024, excluding materials about the reconsideration request.

paragraphs.summary: The court states an amended CTR was filed excluding reconsideration materials.

propositions.text: The Order granting leave in this matter was issued on April 16, 2025.
propositions.quote: The Order granting leave in this matter was issued on April 16, 2025.

paragraphs.summary: The court states leave was granted on April 16, 2025.

propositions.text: The Principal Applicant argues the Officer's decision on wife's full-time student status is unreasonable and should be set aside.
propositions.quote: The Principal Applicant now argues that the decision of the Officer about his wife’s status as a full-time student is unreasonable because it was made without regard to the evidence and should be set aside.

propositions.text: He also submits the Officer breached procedural fairness by denying opportunity to address sufficient funds issue in October 21, 2024 decision.
propositions.quote: He also submits that the Officer breached the duty of procedural fairness by depriving him of the opportunity to address the question of sufficient funds, when making the decision on October 21, 2024.

paragraphs.summary: The Principal Applicant argues the Officer's decision on student status is unreasonable and alleges procedural fairness breach on funds issue.

propositions.text: The Respondent submits the judicial review application is moot since the application was reconsidered and refused on October 21, 2024 with no review filed.
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that the application for judicial review is moot, since the application for an open work permit was reconsidered and refused on October 21, 2024 and no application for leave and judicial review was filed in respect of that decision.

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent argues the judicial review application is moot due to reconsideration refusal and no review filed for that decision.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness issues are reviewable on the standard of correctness, per Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Khosa.
propositions.quote: Any issue of procedural fairness is reviewable on the standard of correctness; see the decision in Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Khosa, [2009] 1 S.C.R. 339.

paragraphs.summary: The court states procedural fairness issues are reviewed on correctness standard per Khosa.

propositions.text: Merits of decision are reviewable on reasonableness standard following Vavilov.
propositions.quote: Following the decision of the Supreme Court of Canada in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov, [2019] 4 S.C.R. 653, the merits of the decision are reviewable on the standard of reasonableness.

paragraphs.summary: The court states merits are reviewed on reasonableness standard following Vavilov.

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires decision to show justification, transparency, intelligibility, and be justified by relevant facts and law per Vavilov.
propositions.quote: In considering reasonableness, the Court is to ask if the decision under review "bears the hallmarks of reasonableness — justification, transparency and intelligibility — and whether it is justified in relation to the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on that decision"; see Vavilov, supra at paragraph 99.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains reasonableness requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and justification by relevant facts and law per Vavilov.

propositions.text: The Principal Applicant seeks orders quashing refusal and inadmissibility decisions and directing grant or redetermination of application.
propositions.quote: In his application, the Principal Applicant seeks the following relief: a) An Order quashing the decision refusing the Applicant’s application pursuant to Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; b) An Order quashing the decision finding the Applicant inadmissible to Canada the pursuant to Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; and b)[sic] An Order directing an officer at the High Commission of Canada, Visa /Study Permit Section, Kenya, to grant the Applicant’s application pursuant to Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; or in the alternative c) An Order referring the matter to another Officer of Citizenship and Immigration Canada, High Commission of Canada, Visa /Study Permit Section, Kenya for re-determination by a different Officer in accordance with the law. d) Such further Orders as this Honourable Court allows.

paragraphs.summary: The Principal Applicant seeks orders quashing refusal and inadmissibility decisions and directing grant or redetermination of application.

propositions.text: Borowski sets a two-step analysis for mootness: live controversy and discretion to hear moot case considering adversarial context, judicial economy, and court role.
propositions.quote: The leading authority on mootness is the Supreme Court of Canada’s decision in Borowski v. Canada (Attorney General), 1989 CanLII 123 (S.C.C.), [1989] 1 S.C.R. 342 (Borowski). Borowski sets out a two-step analysis to determine whether a case is moot and, in the affirmative, whether a court should nonetheless exercise its discretion to hear it. At the first step of the analysis, the court must determine whether a live controversy still exists. If no live controversy exists, the court then moves to the second step of the analysis and considers whether it should nonetheless hear the moot case. The second step of the analysis involves consideration of three factors: the presence of an adversarial context, the concern for judicial economy, and the need for the court to be sensitive to its role as the adjudicative branch in our political framework.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Borowski for a two-step mootness test: live controversy and discretion considering adversarial context, judicial economy, and court role.

propositions.text: Application of mootness principle is a discretionary decision by a court.
propositions.quote: I observe that application of the principle of mootness is a discretionary decision by a Court.

paragraphs.summary: The court states mootness application is discretionary.

propositions.text: Respondent did not raise mootness at leave stage but did so in Further Memorandum.
propositions.quote: In his Memorandum of argument filed at the leave stage, the Respondent did not raise the issue of mootness. He raised the issue in his Further Memorandum.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Respondent raised mootness only in the Further Memorandum, not at leave stage.

propositions.text: The revised CTR excludes reconsideration decision but it is attached as exhibit to Principal Applicant's Further affidavit.
propositions.quote: The revised CTR does not contain the reconsideration decision, but it is attached as an exhibit to the Further affidavit filed by the Principal Applicant.

propositions.text: The Respondent did not object to inclusion of the reconsideration decision exhibit.
propositions.quote: The Respondent did not object to the inclusion of the exhibit.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the reconsideration decision is attached as exhibit to the Further affidavit and Respondent did not object to it.

propositions.text: The reconsideration decision does not identify the decision-maker; this underpins Respondent's mootness argument.
propositions.quote: The “reconsideration” decision does not identify the decision-maker, whether it was the Officer or someone else. This decision is the basis of the Respondent’s argument about mootness.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the reconsideration decision lacks decision-maker identity, which supports Respondent's mootness argument.

propositions.text: The court declines to dismiss the application on grounds of mootness, exercising discretion.
propositions.quote: In this case, I decline to dismiss this application on the grounds of mootness.

paragraphs.summary: The court exercises discretion and declines to dismiss the application as moot.

propositions.text: A live controversy remains between the parties regarding the application for an open work permit.
propositions.quote: a “live controversy” remains between the parties, that is the application for an open work permit.

propositions.text: It is unnecessary to address other elements of the mootness discussion.
propositions.quote: It is not necessary for me to address the other elements of the mootness discussion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds a live controversy remains about the open work permit application and declines to address other mootness elements.

propositions.text: The February 2, 2024 decision was made without regard to the evidence and fails the reasonableness standard.
propositions.quote: the decision of February 2, 2024 was made without regard to the evidence. This means that the decision fails to meet the standard of reasonableness.

propositions.text: The Applicants submit the decision was made without regard to the evidence and is unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I agree with the submissions of the Applicants, that the decision of February 2, 2024 was made without regard to the evidence. This means that the decision fails to meet the standard of reasonableness.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the Applicants that the February 2, 2024 decision ignored evidence and is unreasonable.

propositions.text: It is unnecessary to address procedural fairness issues in this judicial review application.
propositions.quote: It is not necessary for me to address the issue of procedural fairness.

propositions.text: The procedural fairness argument is not appropriately raised in this judicial review application.
propositions.quote: this argument is not appropriately raised in the within application for judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds procedural fairness need not be addressed and that argument is not properly raised here.

propositions.text: The judicial review application is granted, the decision is set aside, and the matter is remitted to a different officer for redetermination.
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review will be granted, the decision will be set aside and the matter will be remitted to a different officer for re-determination.

propositions.text: There is no question for certification.
propositions.quote: There is no question for certification.

paragraphs.summary: The court grants judicial review, sets aside the decision, remits the matter to another officer, and finds no question for certification.
